page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on the Intel Xeon platform using the x86_64 architecture. It allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a 33 MB shared L3 cache, supporting vector acceleration extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512_VNNI. It is provisioned with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a constrained ratio of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, necessitating remote network-attached persistent storage for non-volatile data.

In benchmark assessments, the instance displays midrange multi-core compute capability alongside modest single-core throughput. It achieves a multi-core score of 7430.34 in stress-ng and an overall PassMark CPU score of 8305.34, while single-core metrics register lower, reflecting 1138.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1409.67 in stress-ng single-core. The memory subsystem records uncached read bandwidth of 48.32 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 34.24 GB/sec, though overall PassMark memory performance places in the bottom quartile. Application testing yields 7.13 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 6.62 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The 1:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation establishes clear architectural tradeoffs. While compute-dense operations benefit from full access to dedicated cores and AVX-512 acceleration, applications requiring sizable in-memory data structures face capacity constraints. Cost efficiency is favored in workloads that demand multiple concurrent execution threads without substantial per-thread RAM overhead. Consequently, Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 aligns with batch processing, software compilation, static web traffic handling, CPU-based lightweight model inference, and CI/CD build execution.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz and 8.0 GB of system memory. Built with support for AVX-512 vector extensions and 33 MB of L3 cache, the instance delivers 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU with no bundled local storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmark results place its multi-core compute capacity in the middle tier, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 8305.34 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 7430.34, accompanied by static web serving throughput of 6.62 GB/sec and 7.13 million Redis operations per second. However, single-core speeds and memory performance test in lower percentiles. The tight vCPU-to-memory ratio creates a cost-effective environment for thread-parallel, memory-light tasks, making the configuration well targeted for software compilation pipelines, static web serving, CI/CD workloads, and lightweight inference jobs.
